props.gloss_en: R' Yochanan: one does not pray over an excess of good
R' Yochanan: from where that one does not pray over an excess of good? as it says 'bring the whole tithe into the storehouse...' (Mal 3:10)
what is 'until there is no enough'? Rami bar Rav Yud: until your lips wear out from saying 'enough'
Rami bar Rav Yud: and in the Diaspora they sound the alarm for it [an excess of rain]
in a year whose rains are abundant, the men of the mishmar send to the men of the ma'amad: set your eyes on your brothers in the Diaspora, that their houses not become their graves
until where must rain fall that they pray it not fall? R' Eliezer: so that a man may stand at Keren Ofel and dip his feet in the water
but it is taught [that R' Eliezer said]: his hands
Rabba bar bar Chana: I myself saw Keren Ofel, and an Arab standing there riding a camel with a spear in his hand looked like a worm
'and I will give your rains in their season' (Lev 26:4): [the land] neither drunk nor thirsty, but moderate
for so long as rains are abundant they muddy the land and it does not yield fruit
alternatively: 'in their season' -- on Wednesday nights and on Shabbat nights
for so we found in the days of Shimon ben Shetach that rain fell for them on Wednesday nights and Shabbat nights, until wheat grew like kidneys, barley like olive pits, and lentils like gold dinars
and they tied up a sample of them for the generations, to make known how much sin causes
as it says: 'your iniquities have turned these away, and your sins have withheld the good from you' (Jer 5:25)

and so we found in Herod's days, when they were engaged in building the Temple: rain fell at night, next day the wind blew, the clouds scattered and the sun shone, the people went out to their work, and they knew that the work of Heaven was in their hands

supports.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי: in a year of abundant rain the mishmar asks the ma'amad to pray for the brothers in the Diaspora, that their houses not be their graves
שכן מצינו -- in Shimon ben Shetach's days rain fell on Wednesday and Shabbat nights (kind svara for a 'so we found' precedent; header)
וכן מצינו -- in Herod's days rain fell only at night, and the people went out to their work by day (kind svara; header)
